statement.essentials: A partial superficial parotidectomy removes the tumour with a wider cuff of normal gland than extracapsular dissection, but not the whole outer lobe.
statement.anatomy: Partial superficial parotidectomy removes the tumour with a greater cuff of healthy parotid tissue than extracapsular dissection, and far less than a formal superficial parotidectomy; the facial nerve branches near the tumour are dissected.
statement.clinical: One review would use it for tumours of the caudal part of the gland (ESGS level II) that touch the main trunk, and for large (over 4 cm) caudal tumours that also touch the cervicofacial branch. Removing less healthy tissue than a formal parotidectomy may limit facial nerve dysfunction and Frey syndrome.

limitations: Indications are an author’s recommendation from case series, not trial results; surgeons differ on where partial superficial parotidectomy ends and superficial parotidectomy begins.
